name: ClimbX
tagline: An AI workspace for growing an X account: draft tweets, study competitor accounts, track what performs.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The writing half of this is a one-sitting build: a local drafting workspace with hook templates, an LLM that rewrites your notes into threads, and a queue you approve by hand. The data half is where it falls apart, because reading X programmatically is a paid API problem, not a coding problem, and the tiers that let you pull other accounts' timelines cost more than the subscription you are trying to cancel. You also lose the aggregate view: what is working across many accounts in your niche right now, scored against a corpus you did not have to collect. A personal version that ingests your own analytics export and a manually curated swipe file gets you most of the drafting value and roughly none of the intelligence value. Call it a weekend build with a permanent hole where the reading pipe should be.
coreLoopDIY: A local workspace that turns your notes into tweet and thread drafts against your own swipe file, then tracks performance from your X analytics export.
requirements: Your X analytics CSV export, downloaded manually
A hand-built swipe file of posts you want to imitate
Paid X API access if you want automatic posting or competitor reads
whatYouLose: The cross-account tweet corpus: you only ever see posts you personally saved
Automated audits of other profiles in your niche
Native scheduling and posting without paying for API access
Any signal about what is trending in your niche this week
Mobile capture, so ideas you have away from your laptop go nowhere
moatNotes: The moat is not the AI, it is holding a read pipe into X at a price a single user cannot justify, plus everything previous users have already posted through it.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because X's API is the actual product boundary. Anyone can prompt a model to write a hook, but almost nobody will pay hundreds a month for API access to see what fifty accounts in their niche posted and how it landed. Tools like this amortize that cost across every subscriber and keep the resulting corpus, which is why the competitor-audit and inspiration features are the ones you cannot rebuild. If you only wanted a drafting assistant with a memory of your own voice, you never needed the subscription.
notes: The ghostwriter part is a weekend; the telescope pointed at everyone else is a monthly invoice to X.
prompt:
Build a local-first X (Twitter) growth workspace. Single user, runs on my machine, no accounts, no telemetry.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js 15 App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/climb.db
- Drizzle for schema and migrations
- OpenAI-compatible chat completions, base URL and key from .env (LLM_API_KEY, LLM_BASE_URL, LLM_MODEL)

Data model:
- swipe_posts: text, author_handle, url, my_note, tags, hook_type, saved_at
- drafts: body, kind (single|thread), thread_parts JSON, status (idea|drafting|ready|posted), scheduled_for, source_swipe_id nullable
- posted_metrics: draft_id, posted_at, impressions, likes, replies, reposts, bookmarks, profile_visits
- voice_notes: raw brain-dump text, processed boolean

Features, in scope:
1. Swipe file: paste a post's text, author, and URL by hand, tag it, let the LLM classify the hook type (question, contrarian, listicle, story, data, callout) and store its reasoning.
2. Brain dump box: paste rough thoughts, then a "forge" action that generates three single-tweet options and one thread outline, grounded in my highest-rated swipe posts as few-shot examples. Every draft is editable and nothing auto-publishes.
3. Queue view: drag drafts into ready state with a target date. Copy-to-clipboard button per draft, since posting is manual.
4. Analytics import: file upload for the account analytics CSV that X lets you export. Parse it, match rows to posted drafts by text similarity, fill posted_metrics. Show which hook types earn the most impressions per post for me specifically.
5. A weekly review page: top five and bottom five posts, and an LLM summary of what my winners have in common.

Explicitly out of scope, do not attempt:
- Any X API integration, OAuth, auto-posting, or scraping other accounts. Print a one-line note in the README explaining that reading other profiles requires paid X API access and this build deliberately does not pretend otherwise.
- Multi-user, auth, billing, hosting.

Deliverables: working app on npm run dev, seed script with six example swipe posts, .env.example, and a README that states the honest limitation above in the first paragraph.
